input.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no licence grant anywhere: the only occurrences of "licen[cs]e" are regulatory qualification representations (p0234, p0259, p0272) and the Section 7.5(b) sentence at p0346, which expressly disclaims any obligation on the Servicer to provide, license or assign its servicing software or applications. That is the licence locus for this deal, and as drafted it leaves us with no licensed rights at all, no route to extend rights to our Affiliates, and nothing transferable on a merger or acquisition — squarely the walk-away outcome (rights withheld at the Servicer's discretion with no path to add affiliates). We therefore made the shortest fallback-complete edit inside the same sentence: an affirmative licence to the Issuer and Depositor to use the Servicer's processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications as necessary to service the Receivables, extended to their Affiliates on written notice and transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition. Reconciling the retained disclaimer was necessary because it would otherwise contradict the new grant; we preserved the carve-out for anything the Servicer is restricted from providing by a transfer restriction, confidentiality agreement or legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policy, so the Servicer keeps its protection for third-party and legally restricted materials. We stopped at the fallback and did not add perpetuity, irrevocability, contractor coverage or termination-only-for-breach language. Section 7.4's transition/IP allocation is otherwise untouched, so this does not double-flag the transition obligations.

proposal.summary: Convert the Section 7.5(b) licence disclaimer into an affirmative servicing-software licence to the Issuer and Depositor, extended to their Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor, retaining the third-party/legal restriction carve-out.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the blanket disclaimer of any licence obligation with an affirmative licence to use the Servicer's servicing software and related applications, extended to our Affiliates on written notice and transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition, which is our fallback licence position. We have kept the carve-out for materials the Servicer is legally or contractually restricted from providing.

ops.oldText: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
ops.newText: The Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their Affiliates, a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications as necessary to service the Receivables, transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition; provided that the Servicer will not be obligated to provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
